questions.question: The General Journal is best described as:
options: A dumping ground for forgotten transactions
A book of first entry for transactions no specialised journal accommodates
A replacement for the trial balance
The book where cash sales are recorded

questions.question: Every GJ entry must carry a narration because:
options: It makes the journal longer
The auditors charge per sentence
The GJ records the unusual, so every entry must explain itself
Narrations replace the amounts

questions.question: The GJ's analysis columns for Debtors Control and Creditors Control exist to:
options: Record cash received from debtors
List every debtor's name monthly
Calculate interest automatically
Accumulate amounts for monthly posting to the control accounts

questions.question: N. Mahlangu's irrecoverable debt of R1 100 is written off. The entry is:
options: Debit Bad Debts R1 100; credit Debtors Control R1 100
Debit Debtors Control R1 100; credit Bad Debts R1 100
Debit Bank R1 100; credit Debtors Control R1 100
Debit Bad Debts R1 100; credit Bank R1 100

questions.question: Interest of R60 is charged to T. Pillay for a late account. The entry is:
options: Debit Interest Expense; credit Debtors Control
Debit Debtors Control R60; credit Interest Income R60
Debit Bank R60; credit Interest Income R60
Debit Interest Income R60; credit Debtors Control R60

questions.question: Coastal Wholesalers charges the business R150 interest on its overdue account. The entry is:
options: Debit Creditors Control; credit Interest Income
Debit Bank; credit Creditors Control
Debit Interest Expense R150; credit Creditors Control R150
Debit Interest Income R150; credit Bank R150

questions.question: The owner takes goods costing R480 home. The entry values the drawings at:
options: Selling price, because the goods could have been sold
Half the selling price
Whatever the owner declares
Cost — R480 — because no sale occurred and the owner takes goods, not margin

questions.question: Stationery of R320 was wrongly debited to Trading Stock; the credit to Creditors Control was correct. The correcting entry is:
options: Debit Stationery R320; credit Trading Stock R320
Debit Stationery R320; credit Creditors Control R320
Debit Trading Stock R320; credit Stationery R320
Debit Creditors Control R320; credit Trading Stock R320

questions.question: Redoing the whole original transaction when correcting this error would:
options: Make the books extra safe
Double-count the liability by crediting Creditors Control a second time
Cancel the narration requirement
Have no effect on the books

questions.question: Errors are never erased or painted over because:
options: Erasers are unreliable
The trial balance would detect it anyway
A record that can be altered invisibly cannot be trusted — corrections must be visible, dated and explained
Ink is cheaper than correction fluid

subtopics.title: Control Columns and Posting the GJ

questions.question: At month end, the GJ's control columns post to Debtors Control as:
options: A debit of R60 and a credit of R1 100
A single credit of R1 160
A debit of R1 100 and a credit of R60
Nothing — control accounts ignore the GJ

questions.question: The month's GJ proves itself because total debits and total credits both equal:
With the GJ complete, the six-journal system means:
options: Some transactions may be recorded in two journals
Every transaction in any business finds exactly one front door
The trial balance is no longer needed
Cash transactions now flow through the GJ

questions.question: Mrs Mahlangu's vanished R1 100 falls through to the odd-jobs notebook because:
options: No money moved and nothing was sold, bought or returned — every specialised diary shrugs
It is too large for the other books
The CRJ was already full
Bad debts are recorded twice

questions.question: The column diaries never needed narrations because:
options: Their entries were too small to explain
Their columns were the explanation
Narrations were invented later
They were posted daily

questions.question: Writing a GJ entry is really just:
options: Copying the trial balance
Guessing which account sounds right
The five-step transaction analysis — accounts, classify, direction, sides, equation check
Filling in a printed form

subtopics.title: Three Stories the Big Diaries Can't Tell

questions.question: In the write-off story, what 'died' and what was 'born'?
options: An expense died; an asset was born
The asset (money receivable) died; the Bad Debts expense was born
Cash died; income was born
Nothing changed in the books

questions.question: Lindi's home-shopping is recorded at R480 cost, not the marked-up price, because:
options: The mark-up was too small
Cost is easier to calculate
Drawings are always round numbers
Nothing was sold — there is no profit in carrying your own groceries home

questions.question: The two interest entries teach that lateness:
options: Has a price, charged by the books in both directions without favouritism
Only costs the debtors, never the business
Is ignored until year end
Cancels out between debtors and creditors

questions.question: An audit trail is worth more than perfect-looking books because:
options: Perfect books are illegal
Auditors prefer messy handwriting
Books that show their own dated, explained repairs are books people can believe
Erasing is slower than rewriting

questions.question: The surgeon's rule for corrections says:
options: Rewrite the whole month to be safe
Operate only on the broken leg — correct the wrong leg of the entry and touch nothing else
Corrections may only happen at year end
Always adjust the bank account first

questions.question: After the R320 correction, someone reading the books sees:
options: No trace of anything unusual
A missing page where the error was
Only the original error, unfixed
The mistake, the dated fix beside it, and the honest explanation
